name: Lena Crane
life: “I still remember a first printing with the dedication upside down.” Friday often includes a stop at the public road outside the Port of Asphalt, where Lena can recognize shift change by the lull between two groups of walkers.
voice: I published the book and missed the echo because I never go home to that street.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for an unlined tan jacket and a tiny red thread tied through the lowest buttonhole. Lena has a wide brow and a narrow jaw, with thick, tightly coiled hair. Lena rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket during a conversation.
personality: Lena admires skill and distrusts the idea that skill gives anyone permission to be rude. Lena learns fastest from somebody willing to show how they made a mistake.
agenda: To introduce the publisher to the people behind the echo.
family: Jae Alder is Lena’s younger cousin. Lena brings something that can still be enjoyed tomorrow. Jae checks the date twice. Arrangements do change in their family. Taking a delay seriously without treating it as an insult took both of them years. Asked about *Two portions*, Jae says, “My mother missed parents' nights because she was doing this kind of care.”
connections: Sage Rhodes. Hearing the customer teach makes the publisher rethink the old publicity copy. Also in the story is Darcy Hardy (novelist).
